title: SDK Instrumentation Minimap & Quickrecipes (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical guide for embedding lightweight, production-minded instrumentation into Redwood SDKs and quickstarts. The goal is a one-page "minimap" developers can use to get meaningful telemetry with minimal friction, plus three tiny recipes for common onboarding scenarios (10-minute quickstart, 30-minute lab, CI smoke).

Audience:
- SDK authors (JS/TS, Python, Go)
- Developer advocates creating starter apps
- Solutions engineers validating integration telemetry

Guiding constraints (product & UX):
- Minimal cognitive load: default-instrumented flows should work out-of-the-box with zero config for >80% of users.
- Low overhead: events must be bounded; default sampling only on verbose traces.
- Privacy-first: no PII in events; include clear opt-out.
- Actionable: events and metrics should map to concrete playbooks (alerts, rollbacks, docs).

One-page Minimap (textual):
[ENTRYPOINTS] -> [SDK CLIENT LIFECYCLE] -> [NETWORK LAYER] -> [RUNTIME EVENTS] -> [EXPORT]

ENTRYPOINTS (what we capture by default):
- init: when SDK client is constructed (sdk.version, runtime, env hint)
- auth: first successful call with API key present (hashed key fingerprint, not raw key)
- first_request: first successful inference request (model, mode: streaming|sync|embed)
- error: every non-transient error surfaced to user (http code, error class)
- fallback: automatic fallback to smaller model or region (policy id)
- costsnapshot: periodic cost estimate sample (tokens in/out, model id)

RUNTIME EVENTS (detailed):
- request.start (id, route, model_hint, user_agent)
- request.latency (p50/p95 per route recorded as metrics)
- request.stream_fallback (if streaming failed -> revert to chunked polling)
- cache.hit / cache.miss (prefix cache key, approximate cache latency)
- kvcache.size (approx entries; sampled)

Metric set (suggested names and units):
- sdk.requests.count (counter)
- sdk.requests.latency_ms.p50 (gauge)
- sdk.requests.latency_ms.p95 (gauge)
- sdk.errors.count (counter) with tag error.class
- sdk.fallbacks.count (counter) with tag policy
- sdk.cost.estimated_usd.sample (gauge)
- sdk.cache.hit_rate (ratio, derived)

Sampling & Export policy (defaults):
- Events: send all init/auth/first_request and errors. Sample request.trace at 1% by default (configurable).
- Metrics: aggregate locally and export every 10s (batch).
- Payloads: truncate inputs to 512 chars; do NOT export raw user content.
- Exporters: console (dev), OTLP (prod), optional lightweight server collector (for quickstarts we point to a sandbox collector URL).

Quickrecipes
1) 10-minute Quickstart (developer-facing script)
Goal: instrumented first request that shows in sandbox dashboard\Steps:
- npm install @redwood/sdk
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_<redacted>
- paste the minimal code snippet below and run:

JS example (minimal):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({autoTelemetry: true}); // opt-in default in quickstart
(async () => {
  const r = await client.generate({model: 'redwood-alpha', prompt: 'Hello world'});
  console.log(r.text);
})();

What you should see in ~10s:
- a row in the sandbox dashboard for init/auth/first_request
- latency and cost sample metrics
- a small badge in the quickstart README indicating telemetry connected

Notes for authors:
- Provide a local collector flag (--collector-url) that defaults to the sandbox endpoint for the quickstart build so we avoid sending to prod by mistake.
- Ensure the artifact includes a telemetry privacy blurb in the README.

2) 30-minute Lab: validate retries, fallbacks & streaming
Goal: exercise error paths + fallback model routing and assert telemetry shows fallback counts and streaming fallbacks
Checklist:
- Simulated network failures via env REDWOOD_FAULT_INJECT=latency:2000,drop:0.1
- Run sample app that streams and falls back to chunked polling on error
- Verify events: request.stream_fallback, fallback.policy=region-limited, errors with transient:true tag
- Validate p95 latency increase captured in metrics

Deliverables:
- small test harness in /examples/labs/fallbacks that toggles `REDWOOD_FAULT_INJECT`
- instructions to view the three relevant dashboards (requests, errors, fallbacks)

3) CI smoke (2 minutes):
Goal: ensure SDK shipping in CI emits basic heartbeat metrics to our OTLP test endpoint without sending payloads
Pipeline step:
- install SDK
- run: node ./scripts/ci-heartbeat.js
ci-heartbeat.js should: initialize client with telemetry disabled=false and collector env pointing to OTLP test endpoint, send a single heartbeat (init + auth + ping), then exit.
CI asserts that OTLP collector received an init and a ping event within 30s.

Failure modes & remediation (common):
- No auth event recorded: check env var name mismatch, masked keys, or network egress blocking. Remediation: echo hashed fingerprint locally and test collector connectivity.
- Streaming never falls back: client swallowed error. Remediation: add explicit instrumentation around stream.on('error') to emit stream_fallback.
- High cardinality keys in events: ensure we strip session ids and use stable sampled_id. Review event schema in PR checklist.

Microcopy guidelines (error UX & telemetry consent):
- Errors surfaced to devs should be short + actionable: "Request timed out (2s) — retry with smaller prompt or enable streaming fallback: useClient({streaming: true})"
- Consent opt-out copy for telemetry: "Help improve SDK reliability — share non-sensitive usage metrics. You can opt out with REDWOOD_SDK_TELEMETRY=0."

Rollout gating for instrumentation changes:
- Any schema change that adds new event keys requires: (1) release note, (2) migration guide, (3) deprecation period of 3 releases.
- New high-cardinality tag (e.g., user.email) must be rejected in CI checks.

Developer advocate checklist for quickstarts:
- remove any PII in samples
- make collector sandbox obvious (in big yellow box in README)
- add "how to turn off telemetry" in top-level README with env var
- add expected dashboard screenshots + sample query strings for p95 latency and error rate

Open questions & TODOs:
- telemetry cost budget per customer for hosted sandbox (work with finance)
- standardized hashed-key format across SDKs (proposal in GH PR linked above)
- implement a small in-repo OTEL collector container for offline labs

Next steps (short roadmap):
- ship minimal JS + Python telemetry defaults in next SDK patch (owner: Lina Park, due: 2026-03-01)
- create examples/labs/fallbacks and a CI heartbeat script (owner: Ethan Morales, due: 2026-02-09)
- draft release note and schema migration doc (owner: Priya Nambiar, due: 2026-02-25)

Appendix: quick event schema (flat fields only)
- event.name: string (init|auth|first_request|error|fallback|heartbeat)
- event.ts: iso8601
- event.id: stable-sampled-id
- sdk.version, sdk.lang, env (dev|prod|sandbox)
- model.id, request.mode, route
- error.class, error.message_short (<=140 chars), transient:boolean

End of minimap.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc intentionally compact. Link into the large telemetry design doc once the appendix evolves into a formal schema.
